title: Impact of Softer Economy on Employment of Recent Graduates and Older Workers
what_it_is: Impact of Softer Economy on Employment of Recent Graduates and Older Workers

sections.label: Graduate employment survey findings
sections.summary: The Ministry does not forecast unemployment, and about nine in 10 autonomous university graduates found jobs within six months of final examinations in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The Ministry does not make forecasts of the unemployment rate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Based on the annual Graduate Employment Survey coordinated by the Ministry of Education, around nine in 10 graduates from our autonomous universities found jobs within six months from the completion of their final examinations in 2015.

sections.label: Older resident employment and unemployment
sections.summary: Employment rate for local residents aged 55 to 64 rose to 67.3% in June 2016, while unemployment for those 50 and above rose from 2.1% to 2.3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This has contributed to an increase in the employment rate of local residents aged 55 to 64 to a high of 67.3% in June 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: However, the unemployment rate for local residents aged 50 and above has also increased from 2.1% in September 2014 to 2.3% in September 2016, in other words, an increase of 0.2% over a period of two years.

sections.label: Workers placed aged 50 and above
sections.summary: Of over 11,000 workers placed by Workforce Singapore and e2i career centres in the first nine months of 2016, 39% were aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Out of more than 11,000 workers placed by the Workforce Singapore and the National Trades Union Congress' Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) career centres in the first nine months of 2016, 39% or two out of five successful jobseekers were aged 50 and above.

sections.label: Job fairs for employers
sections.summary: Last year, more than 90 job fairs were conducted for employers to offer job openings to jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For example, last year, we conducted more than 90 job fairs for the employers to offer their job openings to jobseekers.

sections.label: Helping jobseekers find jobs
sections.summary: Out of every three jobseekers needing extra help, about 65%, or two-thirds, were helped to find jobs within the same calendar year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On the whole, out of every three jobseekers coming to us, those who need the extra help, within the same calendar year, we were able to help two-thirds of them, about 65%, to successfully find jobs.

sections.label: Special attention for long-term jobseekers
sections.summary: Jobseekers on the list for six months or longer receive special attention through the Professional Conversion Programme or Career Support Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In other words, if they are on our list for six months or longer, we pay special attention to them, whether it is through the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) or Career Support Programme (CSP).

sections.label: Adapt and Grow initiatives review
sections.summary: The Ministry and agencies including the Ministry of Finance are looking into enhancing Adapt and Grow initiatives in coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In fact, right now, my Ministry, together with the various agencies, including the Ministry of Finance, is looking into what more we can do to further enhance the Adapt and Grow initiatives in the coming years.
